title: Work Tracking Gap Fixes
eyebrow: Redo of background work tracking (parent issue #396): fix every known gap before it reaches main

short.lead: You asked that nothing with a bug or a gap reaches main, including ones older than this pull request. While building I found five. The fixes go on the same pull request (#402, background work tracking), as house-rules 2.73.2. The design loop locks code while a feature is in QA, so it needs a QA failure and a fresh approval before I can edit. I have already moved the six issues back to in progress so that one reply from you covers all of it.
short.hint: Tap a gap to see the fix.
items: The opt-in helper ledger writes an empty file

With HOUSE_RULES_SUBAGENT_LEDGER=on, a finished helper's record in docs/sessions/ lists no commands. The record only starts a new turn when a person sends a message, and a helper never receives one. The fix makes it start a turn the same way the work trail already does. A new check proves a helper's commands appear.
The design loop stores junk in feature names

This thread's feature is stored as "background work tracking 1A 2A</message>": the app's message tag and the page's answer codes stay in the name. A later "QA passed" may then fail to find this feature, or find the wrong one. The fix ends a name at a tag and drops trailing answer codes like 1A 2A. New checks cover both, and a name such as "3D printer" stays whole.
The update check asks for commands that cannot work in a cloud session

In a claude.ai cloud session the plugin is synced from your account, not installed from the aj-house-rules marketplace. So every session starts with an out-of-date banner telling me to run two update commands, and the first one fails with "Marketplace 'aj-house-rules' not found". The fix spots a synced copy and says plainly that it cannot be updated by command here, instead of demanding the commands.
The plugin's own safety commits credit Claude

When a helper goes 10 minutes without committing, the plugin commits its work for it. That commit message ends with "Co-Authored-By: Claude" and a Claude-Session line, which your credit rule forbids. I found one on a helper's branch today (commit 5419ac9); none reached this pull request, because I squashed that branch. The fix ends those commits with "Committed by AJ's agent" instead, and a new check proves it.
The credit guard blocks the project thread link

The guard refuses any GitHub text containing the claude.ai/code/ address. That blocks the "Requested by" link to this project thread, which claude.ai asks every pull request to carry, so the work tracking pull request names the thread without linking it.
Your answer to the credit guard choice below.
One reply moves the loop from QA back to build for these fixes.
Copy the reply from the Wrap-up step.

changes: Starts a turn the same way the work trail does, so a helper's commands appear.
Ends a name at a message tag and drops trailing answer codes.
Names already stored keep their old text until the next approval.
Recognises a copy synced from the claude.ai account.
An out-of-date banner demanding commands that fail.
One line saying this copy is synced and cannot be updated by command here.
A marketplace install on your PC is checked exactly as before.
Credits AJ's agent instead of Claude.
Co-Authored-By: Claude, plus a Claude-Session line.
Matches the line every other commit already uses.
Credit guard (house_rules/safe_git.py), only if you allow thread links
Lets a link to a project thread or session through, and still refuses Claude credit lines.
Links to a project thread, session or artifact pass; "Generated with Claude Code" footers and co-author lines are still refused.
Keeping every address refused leaves the guard as it is.
choices: Should the credit guard let a link to a project thread through?
Yes: allow plain links to a project thread, session or artifact, and keep refusing credit lines and footers
Pull requests can carry the thread link claude.ai asks for, and transcript links can go into issues.
No: keep refusing every claude.ai/code/ address
No change, and pull requests keep naming the thread without a link.
The guard exists to stop Claude taking credit, and a link to your own thread credits nobody.

wrapup.summary: Five gaps found while building background work tracking, four fixed for certain and one up to you, all on the work tracking pull request.
wrapup.changing: Four hook functions and their checks, plus the credit guard if you allow thread links, and the docs.
wrapup.blocking: Your one reply, given in the second to-do item below.
wrapup.next: I build the fixes with a helper, rerun every check, post an updated QA page and swap the issues back to needs review.
